data.description:
# Move fsck's shared filesystem primitives out of `fsck_repair.py`

## Context / Problem

Surfaced by the architectural analysis on `defaceable-icy-antelope` (which split
`_commands/fsck.py` into a command driver, `fsck_scan.py` and `fsck_tracker_health.py`).

Two pure filesystem primitives — `_ticket_dirs` (list the tracker's ticket directories) and
`_resolve_tracker_git_dir` (resolve the tracker's git dir) — live in
`src/rebar/_commands/fsck_repair.py`. They are there for a historical reason, not a structural
one: `fsck_repair` was the first module extracted out of `fsck.py`, and the helpers went along
with the cluster that happened to move first.

The result is an inverted dependency. Neither primitive has anything to do with repair, yet
four consumers now reach into the **repair** module to get them:

- `src/rebar/_commands/fsck_scan.py` — the read-only diagnostic walk;
- `src/rebar/_commands/fsck.py` — re-exports both for module-attribute callers;
- `src/rebar/_store/gitutil.py` — imports `_resolve_tracker_git_dir` (twice, function-local);
- `src/rebar/_commands/fsck_recover.py` — imports `_resolve_tracker_git_dir`.

So a store-layer module (`gitutil`) depends on a command-layer *repair* module to answer 'where
is the tracker's git dir', and the diagnostic path cannot be read without loading the mutating
one. Both primitives are also the sort of thing a future non-fsck caller would want, and would
have no reason to look for under 'repair'.

## Approach

Move `_ticket_dirs` and `_resolve_tracker_git_dir` to a neutral home and repoint the consumers.
Prefer an existing store-layer module over a new one — `_resolve_tracker_git_dir` is a git-dir
resolution question, so `src/rebar/_store/gitutil.py` is the natural owner and already imports
it; if the two primitives do not sit comfortably together there, put both in a small store-layer
module rather than leaving either in `fsck_repair`. Assume the `gitutil` home unless the import
graph makes it circular, in which case use a new `_store` leaf.

Keep `fsck.py`'s existing re-exports so `fsck.<symbol>` attribute access keeps resolving for the
callers and tests that bind to it — that compatibility surface is documented in the
architectural-analysis comment on `defaceable-icy-antelope`.

Behaviour-preserving: no logic change, imports repointed only.

## Testing

No new behaviour; the existing suite is the oracle and is run unmodified. The bindings at risk
are exercised by `tests/interfaces/store/test_event_append_transient_retry.py` and
`tests/interfaces/store/test_stale_lock_reclaim_write.py` (both import
`_resolve_tracker_git_dir` from `fsck`), plus the fsck suites under
`tests/interfaces/store/`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1: `_ticket_dirs` and `_resolve_tracker_git_dir` are no longer defined in
      `src/rebar/_commands/fsck_repair.py` — verified by
      `! grep -qE '^def (_ticket_dirs|_resolve_tracker_git_dir)' src/rebar/_commands/fsck_repair.py`
      exiting 0.
- [ ] AC2: `_store/gitutil.py` and `_commands/fsck_recover.py` no longer import either symbol
      from `fsck_repair` or `fsck` — verified by
      `! grep -rq 'from rebar._commands.fsck.* import _resolve_tracker_git_dir' src/rebar/_store/ src/rebar/_commands/fsck_recover.py`
      exiting 0.
- [ ] AC3: `from rebar._commands import fsck; fsck._resolve_tracker_git_dir` and
      `fsck._ticket_dirs` still resolve — verified by a `python -c` import exiting 0.
- [ ] AC4: no test file is edited — verified by `git diff --stat origin/main -- tests/`
      producing no output.
- [ ] AC5: `make lint`, `make typecheck`,
      `scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py --check` and
      `pytest -m "not integration and not external"` each exit 0.
data.title: fsck's shared filesystem primitives live in the repair module
